pl-l3d37c4-d1e112.summary: Explains that the letter of the Gospel expresses the spiritual understanding which the spiritual have and by which one lives spiritually; the letter of the Law the carnal sense, which the carnal have, and to which something was added.
claims: The Gospel's letter expresses the spiritual sense; the Law's, the carnal.

pl-l3d37c4-d1e115.summary: Gives the third precept, 'you shall not commit adultery', meaning not to unite with anyone outside the covenant of marriage: the part stands for the whole, so every illicit union and unlawful use of the members is forbidden.
claims: Adultery stands for every illicit union outside marriage.

pl-l3d37c4-d1e124.summary: Gives the fourth precept, 'you shall not steal', which forbids sacrilege and every robbery: whoever forbade theft did not permit robbery, but meant by theft every unlawful usurpation of another's property.
claims: Theft includes robbery, sacrilege, and every unlawful taking.

pl-l3d37c4-d1e133.summary: Defines three ways of committing sacrilege: taking something sacred from a sacred place, something non-sacred from a sacred place, or something sacred from a non-sacred place. Whatever is dedicated to divine worship, like a church or its property, is sacred.
claims: Sacrilege is committed in three ways.

pl-l3d37c4-d1e140.summary: Adds that usury, contained under robbery, is also forbidden here.
claims: Usury is a kind of robbery and is forbidden.

pl-l3d37c4-d1e143.summary: Quotes Jerome: seeking usury differs not at all from defrauding or robbing. Lend to your brother and receive what you gave, seeking nothing extra, for any surplus counts as usury.
claims: Usury is no different from fraud or robbery.
Any surplus beyond what was lent is usury.

pl-l3d37c4-d1e152.summary: Gives Augustine's definition: usury is demanding more than one received, whether in money or any thing.
claims: Usury is exacting more than was lent.

pl-l3d37c4-d1e158.summary: Adds Jerome: some think usury is only in money, but any surplus over what was given is usury, as giving ten measures in winter and receiving fifteen at harvest.
claims: Usury is not limited to money.

pl-l3d37c4.summary: Explains that the letter of the Gospel expresses the spiritual understanding by which the spiritual live, the letter of the Law the carnal sense, to which something was added. The third precept, 'you shall not commit adultery', forbids every union outside marriage and every illicit use of the members. The fourth, 'you shall not steal', forbids sacrilege and robbery and every unlawful usurpation of another's property. Sacrilege is committed in three ways, taking sacred from sacred, non-sacred from sacred, or sacred from non-sacred. Usury, included under robbery, is condemned by Jerome and Augustine as demanding more than was given, in money or any thing.
claims: The Gospel's letter expresses the spiritual sense, the Law's letter the carnal.
Adultery includes every illicit sexual union.
Theft includes every unlawful seizing of another's property, including sacrilege.
Usury, demanding more than was given in any thing, is forbidden.
